name: Sign-in and App Shell
summary: Everyone signs in with email and password, lands on the right page for their role, sees only the menu items their role allows, and gets a clear on-page message if they open a page they can't use.

stories.title: Sign in, land on your page, and sign out
stories.plainSummary: You open the app, sign in with your email and password, and land on your role's page (a Visitor on the Contact form, a Support Agent or Admin on the Inbox). If sign-in fails you see a clear message on the sign-in screen, and you can sign out from any page.
acceptanceCriteria: Signing in with a seeded account's correct email and password takes a Visitor to the Contact page and a Support Agent or Admin to the Inbox
Submitting a wrong email or password shows an inline "email or password is incorrect" error on the sign-in screen, keeps the entered email, clears the password and moves focus to the error summary
When sign-in cannot reach the sign-in service, the sign-in screen shows a connection-problem error that is distinct from the wrong-credentials error
While signed out, any app URL typed into the address bar, including the app root, sends the user to the sign-in screen instead of the welcome page or the requested page
After signing out, pressing the browser Back button returns the user to the sign-in screen rather than revealing the previous app page
The sign-in screen has no automated accessibility violations, every field is labelled, and the whole form can be completed with the keyboard alone
manualTestChecklist: Open the app while signed out → you land on the sign-in page, not a welcome page
Sign in as visitor@example.com / Test123 → you land on the Contact page
Sign in as agent@example.com (or admin@example.com) / Test123 → you land on the Inbox
Sign in with the wrong password → you see a message saying the email or password is incorrect, and your email is still filled in
Type the password → it is shown as dots, never as plain text
Sign in, click Sign out, then press the browser Back button → you're sent to sign-in, not back into the app
Using only the Tab and Enter keys, sign in successfully

stories.title: Role-based menu and permission-denied banner
stories.plainSummary: Once signed in, the top menu shows only what your role can use (a Visitor sees Contact and My messages; a Support Agent or Admin sees Inbox). If you open a page your role can't use from a direct link, the page shows a banner explaining which permission you're missing, with a link back to your own page.
acceptanceCriteria: A signed-in Visitor sees exactly "Contact" and "My messages" in the top menu, with no Inbox item shown in any form
A signed-in Support Agent or Admin sees exactly "Inbox" in the top menu, with no Contact or My messages item shown in any form
A Visitor who opens the Inbox address directly sees a permission-denied banner on the page naming the missing permission, and its link takes them back to the Contact page
A Support Agent or Admin who opens the Contact or My messages address directly sees the permission-denied banner, and its link takes them back to the Inbox
The permission-denied banner is announced to screen readers when the page loads and its back link can be reached and followed with the keyboard
manualTestChecklist: Sign in as the Visitor → the top menu shows only Contact and My messages
Sign in as the Support Agent, then the Admin → the top menu shows only Inbox
As the Visitor, type /inbox in the address bar → you see a "you don't have permission" banner on the page (no error page) that names the missing permission
Click the banner's link → you're taken back to the Contact page
As the Support Agent, type /contact in the address bar → you see the banner, and its link takes you to the Inbox
Using only the Tab key, reach the banner's link and press Enter → it takes you to your page

stories.title: Session timeouts and account lockout
stories.plainSummary: Your session ends after 30 minutes without activity, or after 12 hours in total, and you're taken back to the sign-in screen with a message that your session expired. After 5 wrong passwords in a row the account is locked for 15 minutes, and the sign-in screen tells you so.
acceptanceCriteria: On the 5th consecutive failed sign-in for an account, the sign-in screen says the account is locked and for how long (15 minutes)
While an account is locked, signing in with its correct password is refused and the locked message is shown again
Once 15 minutes have passed since the lockout, the account can sign in with the correct password and lands on its role's page
After 30 minutes with no activity, a signed-in user is returned to the sign-in screen with a message that their session expired
A user who keeps working is still signed out with the session-expired message once 12 hours have passed since signing in
manualTestChecklist: Enter the wrong password for agent@example.com five times → the sign-in screen says the account is locked for 15 minutes
While it's locked, enter the correct password → you still can't sign in and see the locked message
Sign in as another seeded user while that account is locked → that user signs in normally

stories.title: Enquiry and user records with sample data
stories.plainSummary: The app holds enquiries and users in memory, starting with sample enquiries that cover every category and every status, so the later Contact, My messages and Inbox screens have data to show. Changes last until the page is reloaded.
acceptanceCriteria: The seeded enquiries include at least one of each Category (Feedback, Question, General Enquiry) and each Status (New, In Progress, Resolved)
Every seeded Resolved enquiry carries a Reply Note, and at least one seeded enquiry was submitted by visitor@example.com
Enquiry records accept only the Category and Status values listed in the brief and enforce the brief's field validation rules
A change made to an enquiry is visible on the next read in the same session, and a fresh load starts again from the seeded data

nonGoals: The Contact form, confirmation page, My messages list, Inbox table, enquiry detail, status changes and delete — later epics deliver these; this epic only routes to their pages and guards access to them.
The reviewer role switcher — dropped by your decision; reviewers sign in as each seeded user instead.
Real authentication, password reset, registration, and account management.
